## Purpose

This procedure describes the operation, decontamination, and
maintenance of the ESCO laminar flow cabinet (clean bench) used in
the EA Program laboratory. The cabinet provides an ISO Class 5
(Class 100) particle-free work environment by passing HEPA-filtered
air across the work surface in a unidirectional (laminar) flow
pattern. It is used for aseptic work that requires protection of the
*sample or product* from airborne contamination, including eDNA
extraction setup, PCR master mix preparation, sterile media
preparation, and filter handling for microplastics analysis.

::: {.callout-important}
A laminar flow cabinet (clean bench) protects the **work** from
contamination. It does **not** protect the **operator** from hazardous
aerosols, pathogens, or chemical vapors. For work involving
biohazardous materials (BSL-2 organisms, human pathogens), a
biological safety cabinet (BSC, Class II) is required. The EA Program
does not currently work with BSL-2 materials, but if the scope changes,
consult the PI and campus biosafety officer.
:::


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All use of the ESCO laminar flow cabinet in SGM 134,
  including eDNA and PCR work, sterile reagent preparation, and
  microplastics filter handling
- **Does not apply to:** Fume hoods (for chemical vapor protection);
  biological safety cabinets (BSC, Class II); field work
- **Location:** SGM 134


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, schedule HEPA filter replacement |
| Lab Manager       | Coordinate annual certification, maintain UV lamp log |
| Trained Personnel | Operate the cabinet per this SOP            |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **UV radiation:** The cabinet may include a UV germicidal lamp for
  surface decontamination. UV-C (254 nm) causes skin burns and eye
  damage. Never operate the UV lamp while hands or face are inside the
  cabinet. The UV lamp must be off and the sash open before working.
- **Electrical:** The cabinet uses high-voltage blower motors.
  Do not modify electrical components.
- **Chemical:** If using ethanol or bleach for surface
  decontamination, follow standard chemical safety precautions.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Lab coat (clean; lint-free preferred for molecular work)
- [ ] Safety glasses (if UV lamp has been recently active, as a
      precaution during the transition)


## Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| ESCO laminar flow cabinet             | SGM 134; horizontal or vertical flow |
| 70% ethanol spray bottle              | For surface decontamination    |
| 10% bleach solution (for eDNA work)   | Destroys residual DNA on surfaces |
| Lint-free wipes (Kimtech or equivalent) | For wiping surfaces          |
| UV germicidal lamp (if installed)     | Built into cabinet; timer-controlled or manual |


## Procedure

### Startup

1. Ensure the UV lamp is off
2. Raise or open the sash to the working position
3. Turn on the blower fan and allow it to run for at least 15 minutes
   before beginning work. This purges the cabinet interior and
   establishes stable laminar flow.
4. While the cabinet purges, wipe down the entire work surface, side
   walls, and interior of the sash with 70% ethanol using lint-free
   wipes. For eDNA work, follow the ethanol wipe with a 10% bleach
   wipe, then a final ethanol wipe to remove bleach residue.
5. Place only the materials needed for the immediate task inside the
   cabinet. Minimize clutter; objects block airflow and create
   turbulence.

::: {.callout-tip}
Arrange items so that clean (sterile) materials are upstream (closer
to the HEPA filter) and used/contaminated items are downstream (closer
to the operator). This prevents contaminated air from passing over
clean surfaces.
:::

### Working in the Cabinet

1. Wear clean nitrile gloves; spray gloves with 70% ethanol before
   reaching into the cabinet
2. Work at least 10 cm from the front edge to stay within the laminar
   flow zone
3. Move slowly and deliberately; rapid arm movements disrupt laminar
   flow and pull room air into the work zone
4. Do not block the air intake grilles (front and/or rear) with
   equipment, paper, or notebooks
5. Do not use open flames (Bunsen burners) inside a laminar flow
   cabinet; they disrupt airflow and can damage the HEPA filter
6. Keep the cabinet running continuously while working; do not turn
   the blower off between tasks during a session

### Shutdown

1. Remove all materials from the cabinet
2. Wipe the work surface with 70% ethanol (and bleach for eDNA work)
3. Lower the sash if applicable
4. Optionally, turn on the UV lamp for 15--30 minutes for surface
   decontamination. Ensure no personnel are exposed to UV light during
   this period. Post a "UV Lamp Active" sign.
5. After UV exposure, turn off the UV lamp
6. Turn off the blower (or leave it running on low if lab policy
   requires continuous operation to maintain cabinet cleanliness)

### UV Lamp Use

1. The UV lamp is a supplemental decontamination tool, not a
   substitute for chemical wipe-down
2. Run the UV lamp for 15--30 minutes after each use session
3. Record UV lamp use in the UV lamp log (posted on the cabinet).
   UV lamps lose efficacy over time; replace after the manufacturer's
   recommended hours (typically 5,000--8,000 hours).
4. Do not rely solely on UV decontamination for eDNA work; chemical
   wipe-down with bleach is more effective at destroying DNA.


## Maintenance

| Task                                  | Frequency              |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------|
| Wipe interior with 70% ethanol        | Before and after each use |
| Bleach wipe (eDNA/PCR work)           | Before and after each use |
| Check blower operation and airflow    | Monthly (hold a tissue at the intake to confirm airflow direction) |
| Replace pre-filter (if present)       | Every 6 months or when visibly dirty |
| HEPA filter certification (by qualified technician) | Annually |
| Replace UV lamp                       | Per manufacturer hours or when annual certification shows reduced germicidal output |


## Quality Control

- Annual HEPA filter certification must confirm that the cabinet meets
  ISO Class 5 (less than 100 particles per ft^3^ at 0.5 um). If it
  fails, the cabinet must not be used for aseptic work until the
  filter is replaced and the cabinet re-certified.
- For eDNA/PCR work: periodically swab the work surface and run a PCR
  negative control to verify that the decontamination procedure is
  effective
- Log all UV lamp hours to track lamp aging


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Used wipes (ethanol/bleach)   | Standard trash                           |
| Used gloves                   | Standard trash                           |
| Spent HEPA or pre-filters     | Standard trash (non-hazardous unless contaminated with biohazardous material) |
| Spent UV lamp                 | Mercury-containing waste; coordinate with campus EH&S for recycling |


## References

- ESCO Corporation. *Laminar Flow Cabinet User Manual*. (Consult for
  model-specific instructions.)
- NSF/ANSI 49. *Biosafety Cabinetry: Design, Construction,
  Performance, and Field Certification*. (Reference standard for
  BSCs; laminar flow cabinets are distinct but share some maintenance
  practices.)

## Training Record

Before operating the laminar flow cabinet independently, personnel
must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Demonstrate proper startup, surface decontamination, and shutdown
3. Demonstrate correct working technique (arm position, airflow
   awareness, material arrangement)
4. For eDNA/PCR users: demonstrate the bleach decontamination protocol
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
